sources.citation: Tedman et al., Efficient experimental characterization of the GPCRome via deep receptor scanning, Nat Commun 2026 (bioRxiv 2025.09.19.677468, PMC12458215)

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface immunostaining with anti-FLAG M1 antibody in non-permeabilized striatal primary dissociated neurons confirmed cell-surface display of the tagged receptor. Receptor signaling function was NOT MEASURED for the FLAG-tagged construct in these studies.
sites.rationale: GPR88 has no endogenous signal peptide; its N-terminus (residues 1–33) is extracellular per the topology landmarks, and the intracellular C-terminus (339–384) is the only other terminus. Because the paper names no specific residue number but the N-terminus is the sole extracellular terminus, position_evidence is topology_derived and insert_after_residue=0 (prepend). The exogenous signal sequence added by the authors is cleaved post-translationally, leaving the FLAG tag on the extracellular face before residue M1. The 33-residue extracellular N-terminal stretch provides ample distance (>3 residues) from the TM1 boundary at residue 34. Full-length human GPR88 expressed in primary striatal neurons with an exogenous signal sequence followed by a FLAG epitope tag prepended to the N-terminus (PMC3732291). Surface display confirmed by anti-FLAG M1 immunostaining of non-permeabilized neurons (L2). A second independent construct (L7, PMC9061749) also places an N-terminal FLAG on full-length GPR88 in pFastbac1 for baculovirus expression, corroborating the same junction.

sources.claim: A cDNA encoding human GPR88 was obtained from cDNA.org and modified using PCR to add a signal sequence followed by Flag epitope tag at the N-terminus.

literature_notes: L1/L2 (PMC3732291) and L7 (PMC9061749) both place a FLAG tag at the N-terminus of full-length GPR88; because they pin the identical junction (position 0, prepend), they constitute one site, with L1/L2 as primary evidence (surface display directly confirmed) and L7 as corroboration. L3–L6 (PMC5871604) report a Venus fluorescent protein fused to the C-terminus of GPR88 with confirmed signaling (BRET assay and knock-in mice); the C-terminus is intracellular (residues 339–384) so this does not qualify as a surface tag site and is recorded in other_positions. L7 also includes a C-terminal His tag, likewise intracellular. No ledger line supports an insertion in any of the three extracellular loops (ECL1 91–113, ECL2 181–191, ECL3 307–318), so no internal sites are proposed.

literature_other_positions.note: Venus fluorescent protein fused to the C-terminus of GPR88 via a 5-aa linker; signaling properties preserved as shown by BRET assay in HEK-293 cells and knock-in mouse characterization, but the C-terminus (residues 339–384) is intracellular and therefore not a surface tag site.
